sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: VIGOROUS SHORTWAVE TROUGH CURRENTLY LOCATED OVER THE NRN ROCKIES EMBEDDED WITHIN BELT OF STRONGER WLYS WILL REACH THE NRN PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON ACCOMPANIED BY A COLD FRONT. A WARM FRONT WILL PRECEDE THE COLD FRONT AND MOVE NWD THROUGH THE ERN DAKOTAS INTO MN.

sections.title: DAKOTAS INTO NWRN MN
sections.text: A 40-50 KT SLY LLJ WILL DEVELOP EWD THROUGH THE DAKOTAS TODAY IN RESPONSE TO FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH EWD-ADVANCING SHORTWAVE TROUGH. THIS FEATURE WILL ADVECT RICHER LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE NWD THROUGH THE DAKOTAS WITH MID-UPPER 60S F DEWPOINTS BENEATH STEEP LAPSE RATES ASSOCIATED WITH AN EWD EXPANDING EML. THESE PROCESSES AND DIABATIC WARMING SHOULD BOOST MLCAPE TO AROUND 2500 J/KG IN PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR. SOME ELEVATED CONVECTION MIGHT BE IN PROGRESS IN ZONE OF ISENTROPIC ASCENT OVER NRN ND. HOWEVER...THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD LIFT NWD INTO CANADA DURING THE MORNING. DESTABILIZATION OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER AND INCREASING DEEP LAYER FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND ATTENDANT COLD FRONT SHOULD CONTRIBUTE TO THUNDERSTORM INITIATION OVER WCNTRL ND BY LATE AFTERNOON. A MID-LEVEL JET ACCOMPANYING THE UPPER TROUGH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO 40-45 KT WLY 0-6 KM SHEAR SUPPORTING SUPERCELLS AS THE INITIAL STORM MODE. PRIMARY THREATS WILL BE VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND...BUT LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS ARE EXPECTED TO BE SUFFICIENT FOR A THREAT OF A FEW LOW-LEVEL MESOCYCLONES AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES BEFORE ACTIVITY EVOLVES INTO LINE SEGMENTS/CLUSTERS AS IT C

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT TODAY WILL BE FOCUSED ACROSS THE DAKOTAS/NW MN...WHILE WEAK FLOW ALOFT AND TYPICAL MID-SUMMER DIURNAL CONVECTION AFFECT THE SOUTHEAST AND THE SRN ROCKIES. A WELL-DEFINED MIDLEVEL TROUGH OVER WRN MT WILL PROGRESS EWD TODAY...REACHING WRN ND THIS EVENING AND NW MN OVERNIGHT. AN ASSOCIATED SURFACE CYCLONE AND COLD FRONT WILL LIKEWISE MOVE EWD ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS TODAY INTO TONIGHT...PROVIDING A FOCUS FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT.

sections.title: DAKOTAS THIS AFTERNOON INTO NW MN TONIGHT
sections.text: IN THE WAKE OF DISSIPATING MORNING CONVECTION...BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS NEAR 70 F WILL SPREAD NWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL/ERN DAKOTAS AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT...AND BENEATH AND PLUME OF ALMOST DRY ADIABATIC MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES. SURFACE HEATING/MIXING AND LIFT ALONG THE FRONT WILL WEAKEN CONVECTIVE INHIBITION AND SUPPORT THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT LATE THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS CENTRAL/ERN ND...WITH STORMS EXPECTED TO BUILD SWD INTO SD DURING THE EVENING. MLCAPE AOA 2500 J/KG AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR NEAR 40 KT WILL FAVOR SEMI-DISCRETE SUPERCELLS INITIALLY...WITH A RISK FOR VERY LARGE HAIL. A COUPLE OF TORNADOES WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE IN THE FIRST FEW HOURS OF STORM DEVELOPMENT...THOUGH MODEST NEAR-GROUND SRH AND TEMPERATURE-DEWPOINT SPREADS OF 20-30 F WILL TEND TO SOMEWHAT LIMIT THE TORNADO RISK. STORMS SHOULD SUBSEQUENTLY GROW INTO TO MORE LINEAR STRUCTURES WITH AN ATTENDANT RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS...IN ADDITION TO THE CONTINUED LARGE HAIL RISK. THE MAGNITUDE OF THE SEVERE STORM RISK WILL DECREASE GRADUALLY TONIGHT AND WITH EWD EXTENT...THOUGH ISOLATED DAMAGING GUSTS AND HAIL MAY STILL OCCUR LATE TONIGHT AS FAR E AS ERN SD AND CENTRAL MN. ..THOMPSON/LEITMAN.. 08/03/2016

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: WATER VAPOR LOOP SHOWS A PROGRESSIVE AND COMPACT UPPER LOW ALONG THE US/CANADIAN BORDER NEAR CTB. THIS FEATURE WILL TRACK EASTWARD TODAY WITH AN ASSOCIATED SURFACE COLD FRONT IMPINGING ON THE WESTERN FRINGE OF SUBSTANTIAL LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE OVER WEST-CENTRAL ND BY MID-AFTERNOON. STRONG HEATING IN THIS REGION AND VERY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL YIELD IMPRESSIVE AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF OVER 3500 J/KG. EFFECTIVE SHEAR VALUES AROUND 35 KNOTS WILL PROMOTE ROTATING STORMS...BUT CONSIDERABLE LARGE-SCALE FORCING ALONG THE SURFACE COLD FRONT WILL LIKELY RESULT IN LINEAR STORM STRUCTURES RATHER EARLY IN THE EVOLUTION OF THE EVENT. VERY LARGE HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO IS POSSIBLE EARLY...WITH WIND AND HAIL AS CONTINUING THREATS THROUGH THE EVENING AS STORMS TRACK EASTWARD INTO THE EASTERN DAKOTAS AND WESTERN MN. ..HART/ROGERS.. 08/03/2016

NO CHANGES ARE MADE TO THE OUTLOOK FOR THIS ISSUANCE. ..BROYLES.. 08/03/2016 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1116 AM CDT WED AUG 03 2016/

outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT REMAINS POSSIBLE ACROSS PARTS OF THE EASTERN DAKOTAS INTO NORTHWEST MINNESOTA THIS EVENING INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS...MAINLY WITH AN ASSOCIATED RISK FOR STRONG SURFACE GUSTS AND LARGE HAIL.

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS
sections.text: AIDED BY AN AREA OF ENHANCED FORCING FOR ASCENT DOWNSTREAM OF THE MID-LEVEL CLOSED LOW/TROUGH PROGRESSING THROUGH SOUTHERN SASKATCHEWAN AND ADJACENT PORTIONS OF THE U.S. PLAINS...INITIAL STORM DEVELOPMENT CONTINUES TO GROW UPSCALE NEAR THE NORTHEASTERN NORTH DAKOTA INTERNATIONAL BORDER AREA. THE INITIATION OF ADDITIONAL NEW STORM DEVELOPMENT APPEARS UNDERWAY WITHIN THE AXIS OF STRONGEST BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION ALONG THE PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH EXTENDING TO THE SOUTH OF THIS ACTIVITY...NOW THROUGH PORTIONS OF WEST CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA AND THE NEBRASKA PANHANDLE. THIS INSTABILITY APPEARS CHARACTERIZED BY CAPE OF 2000-3000+ J/KG...WITHIN A NARROW CORRIDOR OF HIGHER MOISTURE CONTENT ALONG THE TROUGH AXIS...BENEATH STEEP LAPSE RATES ASSOCIATED WITH ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR. AS A MID-LEVEL PERTURBATION LAGGING TO THE WEST OF THE INSTABILITY AXIS GRADUALLY PIVOTS AROUND THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY OF THE MID-LEVEL CLOSED LOW THIS EVENING...A PERIOD OF FURTHER INCREASE IN THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT AND INTENSIFICATION STILL APPEARS POSSIBLE ACROSS AT LEAST PARTS OF THE CENTRAL AND EASTERN DAKOTAS INTO THE 03-06Z TIME FRAME. COINCIDING WITH FURTHER STRENGTHENING OF WEST SOUTHWESTERLY AMBIENT LOW

mesoscale_discussions.summary: INITIAL STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS FORECAST WITHIN THE NEXT TWO HOURS ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE DAKOTAS. WW ISSUANCE WILL BE POSSIBLE IN THE NEXT HOUR OR SO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SURFACE ANALYSES SHOW THE PRE-FRONTAL AIRMASS ACROSS THE DAKOTAS CONTINUING TO BOTH HEAT AND MOISTEN...WITH MIXED-LAYER CAPE NOW INTO THE 2500 TO 3500 J/KG RANGE PER OBJECTIVE ANALYSES AND 18Z/19Z SPECIAL RAOBS. WITH THAT SAID...CAPPING INDICATED BY THE AFOREMENTIONED SOUNDINGS REMAINS IN PLACE -- AS ALSO HINTED AT BY LARGELY SHALLOW CU FIELD STILL IN PLACE ACROSS THE REGION. ONE EXCEPTION IS A STORM WHICH HAS DEVELOPED INVOF THE BLACK HILLS...WITHIN AN AREA OF HIGH-BASED CU/TCU ACROSS NERN WY AND WRN SD IMPLYING ENHANCED LARGE-SCALE ASCENT SPREADING ACROSS THE REGION. ATTM...INCREASINGLY MARGINAL SHEAR WITH SWD EXTENT INTO CENTRAL SD /ALONG WITH AFOREMENTIONED CAPPING/ WOULD SUGGEST ONLY ISOLATED SEVERE RISK ACROSS THIS PORTION OF THE AREA. FARTHER N...EXPECT ASCENT FOCUSED INVOF THE ADVANCING SURFACE COLD FRONT /NOW MOVING ACROSS WRN ND/ TO COMBINE WITH ADDITIONAL HEATING/DESTABILIZATION AND ASSOCIATED CAP EROSION TO RESULT IN MORE WIDESPREAD STORM DEVELOPMENT. WHILE CELLS MAY INITIALLY REMAIN ISOLATED /AND POSE A RISK FOR VERY LARGE HAIL AND POSSIBLY A TORNADO/...FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH THE APPROACHING UPPER LOW FOCUSED LINEARLY ALONG THE FRONT SUGGESTS UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A LINE IS LIKELY TO OCCUR. THUS...RISK FOR WIND DAMAGE SHOULD INCREASE SOME WITH TIME...ALONG WITH CONTINUING POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A FEW REPORTS OF STRONG WIND GUSTS AND HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE ACROSS PARTS OF THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS THROUGH EARLY EVENING. A WATCH IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT SATELLITE AND RADAR TRENDS SHOW AN INCREASE IN TSTMS NEAR/E OF THE HIGH TERRAIN OF SERN WY...WITH TSTMS PROGRESSING TOWARDS THE NEB PANHANDLE. THIS AREA IS POSITIONED ALONG THE SRN FRINGE OF STRONGER WLY FLOW ALOFT...AND EFFECTIVE-LAYER SHEAR ESTIMATED AT 20-30 KTS WILL BE MARGINALLY FAVORABLE FOR TSTM ORGANIZATION. THE PRESENCE OF STEEP LOW-MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AMIDST STRONG BOUNDARY-LAYER MIXING WITH A MORE MOIST AIR MASS WITH EWD PROGRESSION SHOULD CONTINUE TO SUPPORT MAINTENANCE OF TSTMS INTO THE NEB PANHANDLE. STRONG WIND GUSTS AND A FEW REPORTS OF LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE...BUT BOTH THE COVERAGE AND MAGNITUDE OF THE THREAT ARE EXPECTED TO BE TOO MARGINAL FOR WW ISSUANCE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SUPERCELL ACROSS TOWNER COUNTY ND WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A SVR RISK -- INCLUDING TORNADOES -- AS IT MOVES EWD. ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS IS EXPECTED OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SUPERCELL MOVING THROUGH TOWNER COUNTY IN N-CNTRL ND CONTINUES TO SHOW STRONG ROTATION...ALTHOUGH THE STORM HAS TRANSITIONED TO MORE OF AN HP STRUCTURE WITH A PRECIPITATION-FILLED RFD WRAPPING AROUND THE UPDRAFT. THIS STORM IS CURRENTLY THE STRONGEST WITHIN EITHER WW 430 OR 431. SOME INCREASE IN CONVECTIVE COVERAGE IS EXPECTED OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS AS LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT CONTINUES TO SPREAD EWD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS AND THE LLJ INCREASES. MOIST LOW-LEVELS...STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...AND INCREASING MID-LEVEL FLOW WILL SUPPORT STRONG TO SVR STORMS ONCE ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT OCCURS AND THE SVR THREAT ACROSS WW 430 AND WW 431 CONTINUES. ..MOSIER.. 08/03/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SVR RISK WILL ACCOMPANY CONVECTION SPREADING ACROSS PORTIONS OF SRN SD AND NRN NEB THIS EVENING. WW ISSUANCE IS UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A CLUSTER OF TSTMS THAT DEVELOPED WITHIN THE DEEP BOUNDARY LAYER ACROSS PORTIONS OF SWRN SD...NWRN NEB...AND ADJACENT FAR ERN WY...IS FORECAST TO SPREAD EWD/ESEWD THROUGH THE EVENING. THIS ACTIVITY WILL ENCOUNTER INCREASINGLY MOIST/UNSTABLE INFLOW WITH EWD EXTENT...AS IT TRACKS ACROSS A WARM/MOIST SECTOR CHARACTERIZED BY MODERATE TO STRONG BUOYANCY. SLIGHTLY ENHANCED MID-LEVEL FLOW PERIPHERAL TO A SPEED MAX DISPLACED WELL TO THE N OF THE REGION IS SUPPORTING AROUND 25-35 KT OF EFFECTIVE SHEAR. THIS MAY SUPPORT SOME ORGANIZATION TO THE CONVECTION...ESPECIALLY AS A LOW-LEVEL JET STRENGTHENS THIS EVENING. THIS ACTIVITY EARLIER PRODUCED A MEASURED 52-KT WIND GUST AT THE CHADRON NEB ASOS...AND ADDITIONAL ISOLATED SVR WIND GUSTS MAY OCCUR THROUGH THE EVENING. THIS WOULD ESPECIALLY BE THE CASE IF TSTMS WERE TO EVOLVE INTO A MORE ORGANIZED MCS STRUCTURE. HOWEVER...WITH STRONGER LARGE-SCALE ASCENT RESIDING WELL TO THE N OF THE REGION...PROSPECTS FOR A MORE WIDESPREAD SVR RISK SHOULD BE LIMITED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS...HAIL...AND A TORNADO OR TWO CONTINUES ACROSS NRN PORTIONS OF WW 430 /ACROSS NE ND AND ADJACENT FAR NW MN/. A DOWNSTREAM WATCH MAY BE NEEDED WITHIN THE NEXT TWO HOURS ACROSS PORTIONS OF NRN MN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LINE OF STRONG TO SVR TSTMS CONTINUES ACROSS NE ND WITH THE LEADING EDGE OF THE LINE NOW ENTERING FAR NW MN. RECENT SURFACE OBSERVATION AT LANGDON /KD55/ IN FAR NERN ND REPORTED A 40 KT GUST. DAMAGING WIND GUSTS ARE STILL POSSIBLE ALONG THIS LINE...ESPECIALLY WHERE THE CONVECTIVE LINE INTERACTS WITH THE WARM FRONT STRETCHING ACROSS THE REGION. ON THE SRN END OF THE LINE /ACROSS RAMSEY AND EDDY COUNTIES/...STORMS WITH MORE SUPERCELLULAR CHARACTERISTICS EXIST. LOW-LEVEL WINDS HAVE STRENGTHENED DOWNSTREAM OF THIS PORTION OF THE LINE /ACROSS E-CNTRL AND SE ND/ WITH RECENT MVX VAD SAMPLING 0-3 KM SRH OVER 400 M2 PER S2. AS A RESULT...ORGANIZED STORMS WILL LIKELY PERSIST WITH A THREAT FOR ALL SVR HAZARDS...INCLUDING A TORNADO OR TWO. EVENTUAL LINEAR TRANSITION IS EXPECTED ALONG THIS PORTION OF THE LINE. COLD FRONT MOVING ACROSS THE DAKOTAS WILL CONTINUE EWD AND THE LLJ WILL PERSIST THROUGH THE NIGHT...SUGGESTING THE ONGOING ACTIVITY WILL CONTINUE AS IT MOVES EWD INTO NRN MN. AS A RESULT...A DOWNSTREAM WATCH MIGHT BE NEEDED. HOWEVER...LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL BECOME INCREASINGLY DISPLACED FROM THE ONGOING MCS AND THE DEGREE OF DESTABILIZATION AHEAD OF THE MCS IS UNCERTAIN. THESE NEGATIVE FACTORS CAST SOME DOUBT REGARDING THE NEED FOR A DOWNSTREAM WATCH. CURRENT DOWNSTREAM WATCH PROBABILITY IS 40-PERCENT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLD STRONG TO LOCALLY SEVERE GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE FOR THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS BUT A SEVERE TSTM WATCH WILL LIKELY NOT BE NEEDED DUE TO THE CONFINED SPATIAL/MAGNITUDE OF THE THREAT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SQUALL LINE OVER N-CNTRL MN IS CONTINUING TO PROGRESS EWD WITH SURFACE CONDITIONS E OF THE SQUALL LINE CHARACTERIZED BY TEMPS IN THE LOW-MID 70S AND UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS. KPKD OBSERVED A 50-KT GUST AT 0712Z BUT OTHER OBSERVING SITES GENERALLY RECORDED GUSTS IN THE 20-30 KT RANGE. GIVEN THE OBSERVED TRENDS DURING THE PAST HOUR...CURRENT THINKING IS THE STRONGER GUSTS WILL REMAIN RELATIVELY ISOLATED AND THE NEED FOR AN ADDITIONAL SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH WILL BE LOW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLD STRONG TO SEVERE GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE. SHORT-TERM TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR MOSAIC AND 9KM CAPPI DATA INDICATE STORM INTENSIFICATION IS CONTINUING ACROSS E-CNTRL SD. SURFACE OBSERVATIONS DOWNSTREAM OF THE ACTIVITY NEAR THE SD/MN/IA BORDER SHOW TEMPS IN THE MID 70S WITH LOW 70S DEWPOINTS. RAP-PARALLEL FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW APPRECIABLE MLCINH /AROUND -100 J PER KG/ BUT VERY STEEP H7-H5 LAPSE RATES /8 DEG C PER KM/. THE VEERING AND STRENGTHENING WIND PROFILE WITH HEIGHT WILL AID IN STORM ORGANIZATION. IF DEEPER UPDRAFTS CONTINUE TO DEVELOP IN THE LINEAR CLUSTER OF STORMS...THE POTENTIAL CONTRIBUTION FROM WATER-LOADING PROCESSES IN ADDITION TO SOME EVAPORATIVE EFFECTS AROUND H7 AND THE STRONG BACKGROUND WIND PROFILE MAY SUPPORT A GREATER RISK FOR ORGANIZED SEVERE GUSTS THAN PREVIOUSLY ANTICIPATED. WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR SHORT-TERM TRENDS REGARDING THE NEED FOR A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH.
